_comment: THE ONLY definition of a drop: a reel or a TikTok somebody shared into Builda, what was legitimately readable from it, and
the moves that could be made on it. scripts/gen_drops.py emits, all committed:
server/builder/drops_spec.py     (Pydantic, extra='forbid', the door the resolution comes in through)
mobile/src/generated/drops.ts    (TypeScript types + every enum table the phone iterates)
drops/schema.json                (the JSON Schema handed to `claude -p --json-schema`, rooted at DropPlan)
WHAT THIS IS. Two documents in one spec, because they are one round trip. `DropPlan` is written BY A MODEL on the person's
own machine from the text a public link published. `DropResolution` is what the Mac uploads: the facts about the link that
were measured rather than read (which platform, who posted it, how many characters of caption and transcript there were),
the plan if there is one, and the refusal if there is not.
STAMPED FIELDS. A field marked `"stamped": true` is written by the RUNNER, never by the model, and gen_drops.py leaves it
out of the JSON Schema entirely. `Move.verification` is the only one: whether a source URL actually resolves is a fact
about the network, and a model asked to fill in a field called `verified` will fill it in. Every stamped field is nullable,
which the generator asserts, so a document that has not been stamped yet still validates.
THE HONESTY RULE, which is this feature's whole reason to be careful. Every move carries `evidence`: a VERBATIM span of the
resolved text. drops/plan.py drops any move whose evidence is not a substring of what was actually read, the way
analysis/run.py drops a decision pattern whose excerpt it cannot find. A move that names something to install carries a
`source`, and drops/verify.py FETCHES it before the move is ever shown; a source that does not resolve downgrades the move
rather than decorating it. `unknown` and a refusal code are real answers and are the ones to give.
NO FREE PROSE ON THE SERVER'S SIDE OF THE DOOR THAT IS NOT BOUNDED. Every string here names a cap in `max_lengths`. The
three that carry a stranger's words (`title`, `summary`, `evidence`) are the widest, and they are the reason the runner
passes a caption to Claude Code as quoted material rather than as instructions (docs/drops.md, the security notes).
NO DASHES, as everywhere else: no string a person reads may carry an em dash, an en dash, a horizontal bar or a minus
sign. The rule is one function, `analysis/plain.py`, and drops/plan.py calls it rather than restating it.

_comment_enums: drop_status and move_status are not carried by any field here. They are the SERVER ROW's states, and they are in this
table so the phone and the API read one list rather than two that drift (server/builder/routes/drops.py imports them,

MoveSource.name: source_kind
MoveSource.doc: Where the thing lives. `docs_url` is the honest answer for a technique whose only home is a page.

MoveSource.name: ref
MoveSource.doc: How the ecosystem names it: owner/repo, a package name, a formula. Never a sentence.

MoveSource.name: url
MoveSource.doc: The one URL that is fetched before this move is shown. https only.

MoveVerification.name: state
MoveVerification.doc: verified once the URL was fetched and answered; unchecked before the verifier ran.

MoveVerification.name: found_by
MoveVerification.doc: caption when the link was in the reel's own words, search when the find pass went looking.

MoveVerification.name: http_status
MoveVerification.doc: What the fetch answered. Null when nothing was fetched.

MoveVerification.name: refusal
MoveVerification.doc: Why this move is not offered as it was written. A code, never prose.

RecipeIngredient.name: item
RecipeIngredient.doc: The ingredient, as the reel said it.

RecipeIngredient.name: quantity
RecipeIngredient.doc: VERBATIM from the reel: '3 cloves', '1 1/2 cups'. Null when it never said one, which is not zero.

RecipeIngredient.name: note
RecipeIngredient.doc: What is done to it before it goes in: 'minced', 'room temperature'.

RecipeStep.name: text
RecipeStep.doc: One step, one thing to do, in the order it happens.

RecipeStep.name: minutes
RecipeStep.doc: A timer, ONLY when the reel gave one. Null is 'it did not say', and the screen shows no timer.

Recipe.name: serves
Recipe.doc: '4', 'two as a main'. Verbatim, and null when unsaid.

Recipe.name: total_minutes
Recipe.doc: Only when stated. Never the sum of the steps: the reel's own claim or nothing.

Recipe.name: ingredients
Recipe.doc: Every ingredient the reel named, in the order it named them.

Recipe.name: steps
Recipe.doc: The method, one step per entry. The step by step screen is one of these per card.

Recipe.name: equipment
Recipe.doc: Only what the reel showed or named.

Recipe.name: found_url
Recipe.doc: The page this method was taken from, when the video named a dish and gave none. Null when the video published the method itself, and the card says which.

Move.name: move_kind
Move.doc: What the runner would do. `keep` is a real move for something worth remembering and not worth doing.

Move.name: title
Move.doc: The button's words, in the imperative: 'Install it', 'Add it to RideGT'.

Move.name: intent
Move.doc: One sentence saying what done looks like. This becomes the runner's task, so it is specific.

Move.name: evidence
Move.doc: VERBATIM from the caption or the transcript. A move whose evidence is not found there is dropped.

Move.name: target
Move.doc: Where it happens. `existing_repo` means the person picks which one; the model never names a repository.

Move.name: effort
Move.doc: How long it would take, at the coarsest useful grain. Three values, so nobody reads it as an estimate.

Move.name: source
Move.doc: What to install and where it lives. Required in spirit for `install`, and the verifier enforces it.

Move.name: verification
Move.doc: Written by drops/verify.py after fetching `source.url`. Not in the schema the model is given.

DropPlan.name: kind
DropPlan.doc: Exactly one. `unknown` is a real answer and is better than a kind that nearly fits.

DropPlan.name: title
DropPlan.doc: What this is, in the reel's own terms. Not a description of the video.

DropPlan.name: summary
DropPlan.doc: One sentence a builder could act on. No dashes.

DropPlan.name: confidence
DropPlan.doc: 0-100: how sure the kind and the moves are, given how much text there actually was.

DropPlan.name: refusal
DropPlan.doc: Set with kind `unknown` when there is nothing here to act on. Null when there is.

DropPlan.name: moves
DropPlan.doc: Ordered, best first. Zero is correct for a refusal. Five is a ceiling, not a target.

DropPlan.name: recipe
DropPlan.doc: Only when kind is `recipe`, and only from what the reel actually said.

DropPlan.name: tags
DropPlan.doc: Lowercase, one word or two, for filtering the board. Never a sentence.

DropSource.name: platform
DropSource.doc: Which site the link is on. `web` is anything else that published OpenGraph tags.

DropSource.name: url
DropSource.doc: The link as shared, after the tracking parameters were stripped.

DropSource.name: author
DropSource.doc: The handle the platform published. Null when it published none.

DropSource.name: title
DropSource.doc: The post's own title or first caption line, as the platform published it.

DropSource.name: thumbnail_url
DropSource.doc: The poster frame the platform published. Never a frame Builda extracted.

DropSource.name: duration_s
DropSource.doc: How long the video is, when the platform said.

DropSource.name: caption_chars
DropSource.doc: How many characters of caption there were to read. The card shows this when it refuses.

DropSource.name: transcript_chars
DropSource.doc: How many characters of PUBLISHED subtitles there were. Builda transcribes no audio, so 0 is common.

DropSource.name: resolver
DropSource.doc: Which reader got the text. `shared_text` means the link gave nothing and the share sheet's text is all there is.

fields.name: drops_version
fields.doc: == spec version. A stored resolution that cannot say which rules produced it cannot be compared with the next one.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: What was read, and by which reader. Measured, never written by a model.

fields.name: plan
fields.doc: The model's reading. Null when resolution itself refused, and then `refusal` says why.

fields.name: refusal
fields.doc: Why there is no plan. Null when there is one. Both null is a bug and the door rejects it.

fields.name: planner_model
fields.doc: Which model wrote the plan, so two plans a month apart can be told apart.

fields.name: planned_at
fields.doc: When the plan was written. Null when there is no plan.
